thread:
maya: heads-up — noticed a perf regression on a subset of SM95 nodes after the driver update. generation tail latency spikes for seq_len <= 64. :eyes:
kevin: can you paste the probe output and sample cmd you ran?
maya: ran the device probe + microbench harness on a devfarm box:```
./runtest --probe --device=sm95-01 --models=llama-7b --seqs=16,32,64 --profile=kv,kernels
```
maya: profiler excerpt:
```
SM: 95
TensorCore: reported: yes
BF16: hw_ok
FP8: hw_reported: yes but kernel_path=fp32_fallback
KernelPick: wavefront_opt_v2 -> fallback_wave_v1 for seq<=64
KV_hits: -22% (vs baseline)
Latency_p50: +18ms for short sequences
```
devin: interesting — FP8 reported true but kernel_path still falls back. that mismatch can kill kvcache layout assumptions (alignment + lane packing).
kevin: @maya did the driver change align with the platform metadata db? maybe hwcap bit-shift changed and our cap-parser misreads warp/granularity flags.
maya: i diffed the cap blob, looks like driver 537.12 introduced a new "wavefront_flags" field. our cap parser ignores it and assumes old tensor-core tiling -> ends up choosing wavefront_opt_v2 which expects packed KV layout. but runtime falls back to scalar_kernel because kernel handshake fails tls check.
benchbot: perf/regression-alert: job=probe-sm95-01, delta_p50=+12ms, affected=5/32 nodes
kevin: tls check? you mean thread-local handshake on kernel launch that verifies shared memory layout?
maya: yes — kernel handshake reports TLS_OK false for some blocks -> triggers fallback. I captured the kernel handshake logs:
```
[handshake] wavefront_opt_v2: tls_check: expected_shmem=24576 actual=0 -> reject
[launch] falling back to scalar_wave_v1
```
devin: that explains KV eviction. wavefront path expects persistent KV in L2-friendly layout. scalar kernel re-allocs per-request and thrashes the kv cache.
kevin: repro plan: 1) add parsing for new wavefront_flags; 2) synthesize a cap blob with wavefront_flags=legacy and run microbench; 3) run 1% canary on dedicated pool.
maya: tried #2 locally: forcing legacy flag keeps wavefront_opt_v2 alive, KV hit-rate returns to baseline and latency drops.
maya: small patch diff:```
- if (cap & TC_FLAG) use_tc_path();
+ if (cap & TC_FLAG) && !(cap & WAVEFRONT_LEGACY_FLAG) use_tc_path();
```
kevin: looks reasonable but we should avoid hardcoding. add a parser layer that maps the new field -> capability mask with tests. also add a defensive fallback rollback that prefers older kernel for short sequences by policy.
devin: agree. Also add a short-seq microbench in CI that runs seq 1..64 on representative sm95/sm86 combos, so we catch mis-picks.
maya: filed an RFC and PR: https://repo.internal/r/runtime/pulls/8321 (WIP). includes unit tests for cap parsing and a small perf test harness.
kevin: can you include a telemetry tag so we can filter incidents by kernel_pick and handshake_fail?
maya: added telemetry: kernel_pick, handshake_status, cap_blob_version, driver_version. benchbot will aggregate next run.
benchbot: perf/ci-note: microbench added to gate; alert threshold p50_delta > 6ms for seq<=64.
devin: timeline? can we patch prod canary today?
kevin: Ops says we can do a narrow canary on dedicated pool A — schedule at 3pm UTC after the nightly maintenance window.
maya: i'll land the parser + tests this afternoon, push an intermediary feature flag. rollouts: canary -> 5% -> 20% -> full.
kevin: also add a short doc blurb in eng-runtime/wiki about new "wavefront_flags" so infra teams know to expect changes when driver updates.
maya: note for postmortem: runtime should treat unrecognized cap fields as "unknown" (log but don't break kernel handshake), and we need an autosuggest policy that prefers conservative kernel picks on capability uncertainty.
kevin: :thumbsup: great triage. thanks for the quick root-cause.
maya: np — i'll keep the thread updated with bench numbers from canary.
